name: Banh mi
summary: Banh mi is a light baguette with pâté, mayonnaise, pickles, herbs, and usually a protein. The bread should crackle, and the filling should not be only meat.
origin: A colonial-era loaf adapted across the country. Hoi An’s versions are famous; every city has a morning stall. In Da Nang it is the breakfast you eat standing up, on the way to the beach or the Hoi An road.
howToEat: Eat it the morning it is baked. Point at the fillings if the stall has several.

The 16 Apr 2024 Da Nang page describes the Hội An loaf as dense, with a crisp crust, still hot, and a crumb that is slightly sweet on its own. The filling it names is sauce, pâté, char siu, and herbs.
A stall with a queue of office workers is a better sign than a picture menu in five languages.
where: In Hanoi, bánh mì sits with phở bò and bún chả among the three best-known dishes of the city.

In Da Lat, Vietnam National Authority of Tourism does not print a Da Lat-only filling list. Eat it in the morning from a street counter near the market. Stall hours and the price are Check on arrival.

Vietnam Tourism describes a separate Da Lat breakfast, bánh mì xíu mại: a hot bowl of pork-meatball broth, a grilled baguette, shredded papaya, and herbs. Visit Lâm Đồng’s food-tour note prints about 10,000–15,000 VND a bowl and names 26 Hoàng Diệu and 26 Phạm Nhật Duật. Hours for that bowl are Check on arrival.
In Hoi An, street stalls in the old town, the morning of the walk.

Vietnam Tourism’s Hoi An food article says the baguette is at street stalls across town. Its must-try article spreads the loaf with pâté, fresh and pickled vegetables, butter, and sweet chili sauce, and calls it breakfast, lunch, and a snack. The Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 7 June 2023 list names char siu, pâté, mixed beef-and-pork sausage, ham, a butter beaten from egg and oil, and herbs. The 30 October 2024 note names pork, sausage, and herbs. Stall hours are Check on arrival.

In Ho Chi Minh City the sandwich is said to have started here. One account fills the baguette with pâté and chili sauce, then meats, fresh herbs, and pickled vegetables, usually carrot and daikon, and the sauce ties salty, sweet, and spicy flavors. Another lists char siu, homemade pâté, soft butter, pickled papaya, and hot chili, and some cooks add a sauce. A city walk says pickled vegetables and pork. The end of the Bến Thành hall serves bánh mì. Bánh mì Hoa Mã is on Bùi Viện. Bánh mì Huỳnh Hoa is at 26 Lê Thị Riêng.

Fillings to try on the city loaf include shumai, pork skin, fish cake, roasted pork, grilled beef, and shredded chicken. Bakeries that have lasted more than half a century include Bay Ho, Hoa Ma, Huynh Hoa, Tang, Cu Ly, and Sau Le.

In Dong Hoi, bánh mì kẹp bánh bột lọc is a hot split loaf filled with cassava-flour cakes of shrimp and pork, chili cut in threads, herbs, and a thin sweetened fish sauce. Chợ Đồng Hới also fills the loaf with a mung-bean cake.
priceBand: One of the cheapest full meals in the country.
seoDescription: What goes in a banh mi, and how to pick a stall.
